emails.snippet: Hi Store, This email is regarding a CEO escalation wherein the customer has reported that her order was incorrectly placed by the store. We have issued store credit of ₹3199. Kindly assist the customer
emails.body:
Hi Store,

This email is regarding a CEO escalation wherein the customer has reported
that her order was incorrectly placed by the store.

We have issued store credit of ₹3,199. Kindly assist the customer in
placing a new order with the correct prescription and ensure that the Gold
Pro membership is added accordingly.

Customer Registered Number: 9417518382

Additionally, we request you to review the VOC and share a detailed RCA at
the earliest.

Customer VOC:



















*Dear Team,I am extremely frustrated with my experience.Your employee made
a serious mistake by selecting the wrong family member’s prescription
instead of mine while placing the order. Because of this, my glasses were
made incorrectly.Even after that, I was told the order would be delivered,
but now the app shows false status “delivery failed / refused”, which is
not true. No one contacted or attempted delivery.On top of this, I paid
around ₹3100, but only ₹1350 refund is initiated. I am still suffering
because of your team’s mistake, and this is completely unfair.You already
have full history of my case, so I expect:Full refund of my paid
amountProper explanation for wrong delivery updateImmediate resolution
without further delayPlease understand this situation has caused me
unnecessary stress, and I need this resolved urgently.*


*Thanks & Regards**,*
*Ayush Roy*

*CEO Escalation Team | Lenskart.com*

emails.body:
Hello Team,

                    Today I have visited LKST146Malakpet to handle the
troubleshoot. The findings are below customer was escalated that she
ordered glasses through online in 2024 with external prescription from one
of the eye hospital. Since then the child was using same glasses and was
stumbling while walking few times,  2 years later they had the eye test
again at same hospital while checking PGP hospital Optometrist said the
axis were present in glasses was different from their prescription.
Customer came to LKST146 Malakpet store to cross verify  the PGP where
Optometrist from same store found different axis.

On my visit I have cross verified all the three spectacle’s twice and the
power was same as their prescription from Hospital, there is no deviation
neither in axis nor in power. I did all the checks in front of the customer.

RCA: Store optometrist didn’t put the lenses properly on the lens stop  and
didn’t leave the Gimbal( lens holder)  while taking the reading which cause
the deviation Verified through CCTV.

Note: attaching image of Lensometer readings

Regards
Hemalatha
CO APTG

emails.body:
Hi Devendra and team,

We're honestly clueless about what exactly LF is doing with this customer's
order?

   - Initially, this customer placed an order with us on 26th Jan'26 worth
   Rs. 21,999 and since then he has been experiencing quality related
   concerns.
   - Under the latest exchange order (1333016513), the 2nd exchange order -
   the product was aligned to the LF facility and delivered to the store with
   a lens fitting issue.
   - Under QC Failure, the product was sent back to LF twice but the
   results remained unchanged; in both the instances, the product had defects
   and couldn't pass store QC.
   - Even when this customer flagged this to our CEOs requiring meticulous
   quality control, *the third attempt has failed*. The store has again
   received a defective product—this time with scratched lenses—continuing a
   pattern of negligence that is now on its third instance.

*The following images outline the condition of the product as delivered on
the third attempt (via LF):*

[image: image.png] [image: 787336fb-6974-4eae-86ff-0f63c4b9f8d9.png]
Additionally, +Sreejith Kumar C <sreejith.kumar@lenskart.in>  +Binoj S
<binoj.s@lenskart.in> - There was a three-day delay in reporting the QC
failure for the third instance. Despite my team’s close coordination, SM
Prajith failed to inspect the product upon receipt, citing that he '*forgot
to check*' the EGs. This further delayed a resolution for a customer who
has already reached out to our CEOs.

*The customer has reached a breaking point and is now refusing to proceed,
citing serious concerns regarding our production standards and QC
protocols. Despite a ₹22k investment, they have received nothing but
inferior quality products, repeated assurances, and breached deadlines.*

Before we attempt a fourth submission to LF Lab under QC Failure, we
require a definitive confirmation on the following:

   - Can this order be fulfilled with zero defects at LF? If yes, then who
   will own this end to end for ensuring this?
   - If LF cannot guarantee this, we must immediately reroute the order to
   the Manesar or Bhiwadi plant to be processed under KMT’s/Plant Head's
   direct supervision.

+Rachit Jain <rachit.jain@lenskart.in> +Puneet Bahl
<puneet.bahl@lenskart.in> +Maheswari M <maheswari.m@lenskart.com> There's a
dire need of your intervention for bringing this towards closure.

Hi Maheshwari,

This is regarding an ex-employee of Lenskart who had placed Order ID:
1266990086 in February 2023.

The customer recently reported that the eyeglasses case/cover delivered
with the order was small in size and the eyeglasses were not fitting
properly in the case. As a resolution, a John & Jacob leather black
eyeglasses case has been arranged and shipped free of cost.

The shipment has already been dispatched via courier under Tracking Number:
34466717843706 ( Delivery courier). The estimated delivery timeline is 3–4
days, and the same has been communicated to the customer, who has agreed to
the resolution.

Please let me know if any further action is required from our end.


Abhishek Kumar
Cx – Escalation || Team – CEO

“Customer experience is the heart of everything we do.”

always trusted the quality and service that Lenskart represents.

Rim Rectangle John Jacobs JJ E16146-C1 Eyeglasses (Product ID: 211281)”.
The metal legs of the eyeglasses have started developing rust. Due to this,
I am experiencing skin irritation and rashes where the frame comes in
contact with my skin.

replacement a few months ago. Unfortunately, the same problem has occurred
again with the replacement pair, and the rusting seems to be getting worse.

such material issues in eyewear can potentially lead to skin problems or
infections for customers who use the product daily. Eyeglasses remain in
constant contact with the skin, and any corrosion or rusting in the
material can pose hygiene and health concerns.

As a loyal customer who genuinely appreciates the Lenskart brand, my
intention in writing this email is to ensure that this issue receives
attention and that the product quality is reviewed to prevent similar
experiences for other customers.

I would sincerely appreciate your support in resolving this matter and
guiding me on the next steps.

Thank you for your time and attention.

Regards,

Chanakhya Srinivas Alamanda

raised concerns about the frame being old or purchased from another store.

incorrect and misleading. I have evidence to substantiate this and am
prepared to present it to Mr. Peyush if required.

from the call center representatives (Mr. Ankit & Mr. Abhishek). I do not
wish to continue receiving generic responses that do not address the actual
concern.

Further, I have observed a quality difference in lens finishing. The blue
coating, which your store claimed or implied as part of professional
standards, was not properly provided, whereas the other store delivered it
clearly and visibly.

This entire experience has been extremely disappointing and has seriously
impacted my trust in your brand. I request immediate attention from senior
management and a genuine review of this matter.

Regards,

Somnathshastry Samavedam

If we lose a Non-LK frame while taking it for repair/Lens replacement ( I
understand these are the only two options) , we are giving the exact amount
of the frame value .Whether new or old, we have no right to value the
customer's frame based on age or any other factor.

so full re-imbursement irrespective of age is my answer

Now on support missing contextual evidence to expedite the pacification
process. Regardless of the communication medium, we need a single source of
truth in one place. I know you are evaluating CRM tools. The Tool should
prevent the support team from making mistakes; otherwise, the blaming game
will continue

One CS agent handling a case end-to-end is one of the solutions I propose.
If that CS agent is on leave, a micro team should form, and knowledge
transfer (KT)/information sharing must happen diligently.

Also, I do not have an answer right now on how to ensure store & CS are on
the same page ( I would love to do it via tech)

And thanks for the response after 15 days

emails.snippet: Hi Ramneek Sir and Maheswari, The customer submitted the bill for their own frame, went till CS head for resolution — still we gave ₹10K voucher when the bill states ₹36K – Rachit/Jayendra First,
emails.body:
Hi Ramneek Sir and Maheswari,



The customer submitted the bill for their own frame, went till CS head for
resolution — still we gave ₹10K voucher when the bill states ₹36K –
Rachit/Jayendra



First, regarding the compensation: The customer’s frame was lost in
transit. As per policy, the standard offering for loss of customer-owned
frames is ₹5,000 GV which customers sign up for at the time of going for
repair and lens only orders.



However, since the customer requested full reimbursement and shared an
invoice, we conducted a detailed sanity check. During the review, we
identified that the invoice submitted was over 10 years old.



Considering the significantly depreciated value of the frame and usage over
a decade, restoration to original purchase price is not commercially or
policy aligned. Historical purchase value does not equate to current
recoverable value for a used personal item.



As a customer-centric exception, we approved a ₹10,000 GV — which is 2x the
standard policy offering. This was not a random decision but a calibrated
exception after evaluating:

• Policy guidelines
• Invoice age (10+ years)
• Depreciation
• Precedent risk
• Overall commercial impact



It was a conscious decision to go beyond policy, not to deny value.



Separately, in our last Monday discussion, Maheshwari was to revert with
clarity on whether we want to redefine handling for cases where invoice age
exceeds a certain threshold and whether complete reimbursement should be
considered in such scenarios.



@Maheswari M <maheswari.m@lenskart.com> – please confirm how you would like
us to take this forward:

• Should we define a structured depreciation grid linked to invoice age?
• Or should invoices beyond X years qualify for full reimbursement
irrespective of age?
• Or do we continue with capped exception logic?



Aligning this structurally will prevent future ambiguity and escalation.



L1 support team acted on the case without checking the history –
Rachit/Jayendra



Post detailed audit of all linked tickets and case IDs, the compensation
decision was not taken without reviewing history.



Timeline clarity:

• On 16th December, the Email team correctly communicated the standard
policy of ₹5,000 GV for loss of customer-owned frames.
• On 24th December, once the invoice was shared, the case was escalated
internally to Rachit/Jayendra for exception guidance.
• The invoice value (~₹36K) and purchase year were reviewed before any
direction was given.

It was a 10-year-old frame; hence, we went the extra mile and made an
exception beyond policy.



There was no independent L1 decision to alter compensation without
leadership review. The ₹10,000 approval was given after assessing:

• Policy cap (₹5,000 standard)
• Invoice age (over 10 years old)
• Depreciation logic for long-used personal goods
• Precedent and commercial sustainability



Where L1 did fall short:

• Some responses were repetitive and lacked contextual summary.
• Closure happened without successful verbal confirmation in one instance.

So the gap was operational continuity and communication discipline — not
absence of history review while deciding compensation.



*How many people from customer support will handle the same case? –
Rachit/Jayendra*



Customers reach out via multiple channels — Store, Email, CTT, CEO
Escalation, and Voice — each with different routing logic.



Handling rules:

• Chat – Same-agent routing applies only if the advisor is available and
interaction is same-day. We cannot make customers wait for a specific
advisor if they are unavailable.
• Email / CEO / CTT – If the same agent is available, reassignment
typically flows back. However, this depends on shift rosters, queue
balancing, SLA risk, and leave schedules.
• Voice – Real-time channel. One agent handles one call at a time. Calls
must connect to the next available advisor; we cannot hold customers in
queue waiting for a specific agent.



In this case:

• Customer contacted us across multiple days (not a single continuous
interaction).
• Engagement happened through Store as well, which runs a parallel workflow.
• Holiday gaps and reassignment logic led to multiple advisors touching the
case.



Multiple handlers occurred due to multi-day, multi-channel engagement and
availability constraints.



Best Regards,

Jayendra Giri

First, regarding the compensation: The customer’s frame was lost in
transit. As per policy, the standard offering for loss of customer-owned
frames is ₹5,000 GV which customers sign up for at the time of going for
repair and lens only orders.

However, since the customer requested full reimbursement and shared an
invoice, we conducted a detailed sanity check. During the review, we
identified that the invoice submitted was over 10 years old.

Considering the significantly depreciated value of the frame and usage over
a decade, restoration to original purchase price is not commercially or
policy aligned. Historical purchase value does not equate to current
recoverable value for a used personal item.

As a customer-centric exception, we approved a ₹10,000 GV — which is 2x the
standard policy offering. This was not a random decision but a calibrated
exception after evaluating:
* Policy guidelines
* Invoice age (10+ years)
* Depreciation
* Precedent risk
* Overall commercial impact

It was a conscious decision to go beyond policy, not to deny value.

 Separately, in our last Monday discussion, Maheshwari was to revert with
clarity on whether we want to redefine handling for cases where invoice age
exceeds a certain threshold and whether complete reimbursement should be
considered in such scenarios.

@Maheswari M – please confirm how you would like us to take this forward:
* Should we define a structured depreciation grid linked to invoice age?
* Or should invoices beyond X years qualify for full reimbursement
irrespective of age?
* Or do we continue with capped exception logic?

Aligning this structurally will prevent future ambiguity and escalation.

L1 support team acted on the case without checking the history –
Rachit/Jayendra

Post detailed audit of all linked tickets and case IDs, the compensation
decision was not taken without reviewing history.

Timeline clarity:
* On 16th December, the Email team correctly communicated the standard
policy of ₹5,000 GV for loss of customer-owned frames.
* On 24th December, once the invoice was shared, the case was escalated
internally to Rachit/Jayendra for exception guidance.
* The invoice value (~₹36K) and purchase year were reviewed before any
direction was given.
It was a 10-year-old frame; hence, we went the extra mile and made an
exception beyond policy.

There was no independent L1 decision to alter compensation without
leadership review. The ₹10,000 approval was given after assessing:
* Policy cap (₹5,000 standard)
* Invoice age (over 10 years old)
* Depreciation logic for long-used personal goods
* Precedent and commercial sustainability

Where L1 did fall short:
* Some responses were repetitive and lacked contextual summary.
* Closure happened without successful verbal confirmation in one instance.
So the gap was operational continuity and communication discipline — not
absence of history review while deciding compensation.

How many people from customer support will handle the same case? –
Rachit/Jayendra

Customers reach out via multiple channels — Store, Email, CTT, CEO
Escalation, and Voice — each with different routing logic.

Handling rules:
* Chat – Same-agent routing applies only if the advisor is available and
interaction is same-day. We cannot make customers wait for a specific
advisor if they are unavailable.
* Email / CEO / CTT – If the same agent is available, reassignment
typically flows back. However, this depends on shift rosters, queue
balancing, SLA risk, and leave schedules.
* Voice – Real-time channel. One agent handles one call at a time. Calls
must connect to the next available advisor; we cannot hold customers in
queue waiting for a specific agent.

In this case:
* Customer contacted us across multiple days (not a single continuous
interaction).
* Engagement happened through Store as well, which runs a parallel workflow.
* Holiday gaps and reassignment logic led to multiple advisors touching the
case.

Multiple handlers occurred due to multi-day, multi-channel engagement and
availability constraints.

Best Regards,
Jayendra Giri

emails.snippet: Hi Maheswari and Nitin Sir, Sincere apologies for the delayed response on this order. At the time of escalation, we had already reviewed and discussed the case; however, we were unable to identify the
emails.body:
Hi Maheswari and Nitin Sir,

Sincere apologies for the delayed response on this order. At the time of
escalation, we had already reviewed and discussed the case; however, we
were unable to identify the exact root cause. Therefore, the issue was
escalated to the Tech team for better clarity.

*Please find the Ops RCA below:*

*1. PFU Ownership Criteria:*
Orders come under PFU ownership only when the order status is *Power Follow
Up*. We can identify and work only on orders that are in this status.

*2. Power Update by PFU Team:*
In this case, the customer uploaded the prescription, and *Nishali Gandhi
(PFU Team)* updated the powers as per the prescription and mentioned that *PD
was required*.

*3. Multiple Changes by Customer:*
After this, the customer made multiple changes by manually updating the
powers and re-uploading prescriptions. Because of these repeated updates,
we are unable to clearly identify which powers were updated by the PFU team
and which were updated by the customer.

*4. VSM Tracking Limitation:*
Currently, VSM captures events at the *order level*, not at the *PID level*.
For example, even if the power is updated for only one PID, VSM shows the
event as *“Power Updated”* for the entire order. This makes it difficult to
track exact changes for each individual PID.

*5. Edit Power Access After Order Processing:*
The customer still had access to edit the power even after the order was
processed. This issue has been raised earlier as well. Ideally, power edit
access should be restricted once the order is processed and only allowed to
advisors, and that too before the *Picked stage*, if strictly required.

*6. Conclusion:*
Due to the above system limitations and multiple manual updates, we are
unable to accurately identify PID-level power update actions. For proper
event clarity and tracking, *technical intervention is required.*

Please let us know if any further details are needed.
*Bhim Bhusal*
*Team Leader, PFU – Lenskart*

Hi Nitin and Team,

Please check this issue highlighted by one of our store -

*Store Code: *LKST2196
*Concerned Order: *1332207995

*Problem Statement: *On 20th Feb'26 Customer has purchased LK studio frame
with Owndays blu+ISHEILD(order no.1332207995) lenses but when the customer
logged in on Owndays website via QR given with the order the lens
specifications is showing Owndays normal vision and the customer has raised
concern regarding this need clarification on this.

[image: image.png]

We’ve identified a technical discrepancy where scanning our QR codes pulls
package details from the backend field rather than the "Customer Package"
frontend field. This inconsistency is causing significant confusion between
Customer Service and Store teams, ultimately hurting the customer
experience.

*To resolve this ahead of Maheswari’s store call tomorrow, please provide
- *

   1. A comprehensive list of all Owndays packages, mapped by Frontend Name
   vs. Backend Name.
   2. The rationale behind maintaining two different naming versions for
   the same product if
   3. If there are any challenges around having one common name - for both
   Frontend & Backend.

We need to address these points on priority to streamline our operations.
If you are not the right point of contact for this, please loop in the
relevant stakeholder immediately. Thanks!
-- 
[image: Kind regards,]
[image: "created with MySignature.io"]
Karan Kumar

emails.body:
Hi Maheswari,

This is a ongoing case, here is the RCA.

Observation :

   -

   The customer, Manthu, was using his previous prescription, which was
   tested at an eye hospital in Sep’23, and he was comfortable with those
   powers. Using the same prescription, he purchased his last product on 30th
   Nov’25 under Order ID 1325122577.
   -

   On 28th Dec’25, he purchased a free lens replacement voucher under Order
   ID 1327410804 and received the voucher code FRLENSB-JZEEPI3V.
   -

   Subsequently, he visited the Lenskart store at Tinsukia, Assam (ST611)
   and underwent an eye test. The store provided the prescription as RE:
   -2.75 D and LE: -2.25 D, whereas he was earlier using RE: -2.00 D and LE:
   -2.75 D.
   -

   After completion of the eye test, the customer submitted his frame and
   placed a lenses-only order under Order ID 1327420507, which was
   delivered to him on 5th Jan’26.
   -

   After receiving the glasses, he continued using them and experienced blurry
   vision and headaches. He assumed that, as they were new glasses, it
   might take a few days to adjust, and therefore continued using them for
   nearly a month. When the issue did not resolve, he checked the Lenskart app
   and compared the prescription of the new order with his previous orders,
   after which he realized that the store had provided different powers.
   However, he did not report the power-related issue to the store at that
   time.
   -

   On 8th Feb '26, the customer directly sent an email to email
Support and Ashwani
   Agarwal citing that the store had given the wrong powers. We received
   the email and created a manual case under Case ID 117147513.


Action Taken:

   -

   Spoke with the customer and apologized for the inconvenience caused.
   -

   Arranged a cluster optometrist visit for a fresh eye test on Tuesday and
   got completed.
   -

   The optometry team conducted the eye test and confirmed that the
   customer’s power remains the same as what he has been using since 2023.
   -

   It was identified that the store staff had inadvertently swapped the
   power values while saving the prescription in the Power Bank system after
   the eye test.
   -

   Offered replacement of lenses with the correct prescription along with
   complimentary glasses as a goodwill gesture.


------------------------------

Customer’s Demand & Resolution Shared:Initial Customer Request:

   -

   Replacement of current lenses with an upgraded package (from Blu Screen
   Lenses to Owndays Japan Blu + iShield) free of cost.
   -

   Two John Jacobs frames along with Owndays Japan Blu + iShield lenses.
   -

   Reimbursement of medical bills.

Resolution Offered by Us:

   -

   Replacement of current lenses with the same Blu Screen lens package.
   -

   One complimentary eyeglass (Lenskart Air / Vincent Chase) with Blu
   Screen lenses worth ₹2,500.


Current Customer Request:

   -

   Replacement of current lenses with Owndays Japan Blu + iShield.
   -

   One Owndays frame with Owndays Japan Blu + iShield lenses.
   -

   Reimbursement of medical bills.



Attaching the Eye-Test RCA as well.

emails.subject: CEO Esc: Review Item | 1327117064 | 115831237 | Process Clarification: Gate Pass Sequences
emails.snippet: Hi Nitin, I'd like to request a review of our Gate-Pass (GP) process following a recent error. Our store team accidentally sent a customer's frame to the warehouse using the wrong GP.
emails.body:
Hi Nitin,

I’d like to request a review of our Gate-Pass (GP) process following a
recent error. Our store team accidentally sent a customer's frame to the
warehouse using the wrong GP. Consequently, the warehouse team could not
link the frame to the correct order and mistakenly routed it for
refurbishment.


*To prevent this from happening again, could you clarify the following:*
*Sequence Distinction: *Do we currently use different GP sequences to
distinguish between "Lens Only" orders and frames sent via
"Return/Exchange" requests?

*Process Fix: *If there is no existing distinction, what system-driven
controls can we implement to ensure frames are correctly identified upon
arrival at the warehouse?
--

emails.body:
Hi Karan,

As checked, the above-mentioned order was canceled due to a missing frame
in the GP.

As per the Returns Team, the frame was not sent in the assigned GP. The
Returns Team from Manesar Warehouse had already informed the store via
email regarding the missing frame in the GP. Hence, no call was made on
this data, as the stores had already been informed by the Returns Manesar
team for these orders.

Based on this confirmation, the order was updated for cancellation by the
Returns Warehouse Team (Vishal Mishra) on 1st January, and the order was
successfully canceled on 2nd January.

Please find the attached screenshot, where you can view the order along
with the reason for cancellation, including confirmation that the
information was shared with the store at the same time.


[image: image.png]

emails.snippet: Hi Team, We would like to request a system enhancement in the Store POS (iPad) to improve store efficiency and customer experience. Currently, when a customer requests the same frame, and it is not
emails.body:
Hi Team,

We would like to request a system enhancement in the Store POS (iPad) to
improve store efficiency and customer experience.

Currently, when a customer requests the same frame, and it is not available
in stock, the store team has limited support in suggesting close
alternatives immediately.

*We propose that:*

   -

   When the customer’s frame is scanned, and the exact frame is unavailable,
   -

   The iPad should automatically display similar frames available in stock
   (based on model, size, shape, color, price range, or category).

We have also received a CEO escalation in recent days due to this
limitation, where the store was unable to suggest a similar PID to the
customer when the requested frame was unavailable. This directly impacted
customer experience and led to escalation.

*This enhancement will:*

   -

   Help store staff offer instant alternatives
   -

   Reduce dependency on manual searching
   -

   Improve conversion at the store level
   -

   Enhance overall customer experience
   -

   Minimize unnecessary follow-ups or escalations

Kindly review the feasibility of adding this feature and share the possible
timelines. Please let us know if any additional inputs are required from
our end.

Looking forward to your support on this.

Order No CEO Ticket
1284405843 113952784

-- 
*Regards, *
Abhishek Yadav
Manager | CS- Lenskart.com
Email | abhishek.yadav@thelenskart.com
Mobile |
+91 8742940151

emails.subject: System Enhancement Request – Mandatory Customer Name Field to Avoid Escalations
emails.snippet: Hi Team, We would like to highlight a recent CEO escalation we received, wherein a customer's order was shipped under the name “Guest User”, and the invoice was also generated with the same name.
emails.body:
Hi Team,

We would like to highlight a recent CEO escalation we received, wherein a
customer’s order was shipped under the name *“Guest User”*, and the invoice
was also generated with the same name. This directly resulted in customer
dissatisfaction and escalation at the CEO level.

*To prevent recurrence of such cases, we request a system-level validation
enhancement:*

   -

   At the time of placing an order (via Store or Online), the Customer Name
   field should be made mandatory.
   -

   The system should not allow the order to proceed if the name field is
   left blank.
   -

   Default values such as “Guest User” should be restricted.

*Implementing this validation will:*

   -

   Ensure accurate invoice generation
   -

   Maintain correct customer database records
   -

   Avoid confusion at the time of delivery
   -

   Prevent issues during reimbursement claims or official submissions
   -

   Reduce unnecessary escalations

Requesting the Tech team to review the feasibility and implement this
change at the earliest to strengthen process accuracy and customer
experience.

Please let us know if any additional details are required from our end.


Order No CEO Ticket
1325077854 113941690
[image: image.png]


-- 
*Regards, *
Abhishek Yadav
Manager | CS- Lenskart.com
Email | abhishek.yadav@thelenskart.com
Mobile |
+91 8742940151

Hi Shitij,

Sharing customer feedback for your review and consideration.

The customer has addressed Mr. Peyush Bansal regarding his experience and
highlighted the unavailability of the Wayfarer Clip-on model in the 145mm
size. The customer mentioned that he visited multiple stores, where the
store teams confirmed that this specific size and model combination is
currently not part of the clip-on inventory.

The customer further shared that the available sizes (137mm–142mm) do not
provide a proper fit due to a broader face profile. He expressed a specific
demand for a 145mm size in the Wayfarer Clip-on range, indicating a
potential requirement for larger frame sizes within this category.

Requesting you to please review this feedback from a merchandising
perspective and consider if this can be evaluated for future assortment

Dear team
 I did not want to give these progressive lenses to the customer because
the customer's health was not good, he was a bed rest customer, I had told
this to the customer in the beginning itself that you will face problem
with these progressive lenses… The customer did not listen to me and he
made the progressive lenses… Two-four days after the specs arrived, the
customer called and said that there is a vision problem with the specs, you
should visit once… I went to the customer's house on 15th or 16th movement…
and explained to him that it takes time to get set, you should use it
daily, the customer agreed… then the customer called and said no, change
it… I went to the customer's house on 25th November and asked for exchange,
I did not exchange the customer I had to refund... so I took the
specifications from the customer which was only one frame, one frame was
buy back... I tried for refund on 28th November but there was no refund
option... then I called my AM and told him that refund option is not coming
then he told me that refund is not available in buy back option... ticket
of this order ID will have to be renewed... I told this to the customer
that it will take some time for refund because refund takes time due to buy
back option. I gave time till 15th December to CX for refund... ticket was
renewed on 1st... I went on holiday from 3rd December to 7th December...
cheque was renewed on 9th I got the ticket cancelled and then got a call
from the customer team on 12th December that you will have to deliver this
frame to the warehouse and send it to some gate pass. Then I told the
customer everything and told him that it is taking time sir, the refund
will come by 25th December. In this entire case, I never ignored any of the
customer's messages or calls. All this happened due to a mistake, I did not
have the idea of buy back refund.

emails.body:
Hi Maheswari

The image doesn’t show any rainbow in the lens view. Only minor colour
change that i see is on the last edge of 2-3 mm.

- As per ANSI there should be no issues in the vision zone which is centre
30mm. In lenskart we consider defects of complete lens if it impacts vision.
- the clip on has a polarised tac lens and it rotates the scattered lights
to clarify the vision for the wearer. In shared images, the images are
taken inside the room and against a bright light. Polarisation is given to
viewers for enhancing vision in outside environment.

These were the reasons given by Kiran as explanation to the CS team and
mail has been sent in agreement of both teams. I do not understand the
reason of disconnect here. Neither any clarification has been sought on any
features so far nor the changes have been done unanimously.

If the SME advise is not acceptable, team could always seek further
clarification or discuss with another expert in the organisation from
category teams.

Regards,
Ruchi Nagpal

emails.body:
Hi,

Customer purchases OD Frame (4900) with BLU Thin+ (2500) and Ultra Thin
Coating (2500) - Total 4900+ 2500 + 2500 = 9900. So during Exchange he can
claim worth 9900

Then frame he chose Fossil. Fossil is 6800 frame + 5000 package with
coating - Total 6800 + 5000 = 11800

11800 - 9900 = 1900. Hence 1900 he has to pay extra

Okay we will proceed with this replacement for now. @Elaine
<tan.yun@lenskart.sg> please proceed.

However, I do not think that the assessment done online will be better than
the assessment done on the ground. My team has a strict policy to follow so
that we set the right expectations to both staff and customers.

I hope that there will be no commitment to any customers without the
knowledge or alignment from the local team in future so that we will seem
as one organisation and not disjointed.

Thank you.

Hi Elaine, Jarrod, and Team,

Thank you for the detailed discussion and for sharing your perspectives.

To provide clarity on the decision: this particular order was within three
months of purchase, and the concern raised was related to a hinge breakage.
As per our existing guidelines, hinge-related issues fall into a grey area,
where it is often challenging to conclusively differentiate between
manufacturing defect and early wear-and-tear without physical inspection
over time.

Considering the early lifecycle of the product, the nature of the issue,
and the overall customer experience, an exceptional call was taken in this
case purely from a customer delight standpoint. This approval was not
intended to override policy or set a blanket precedent, but rather to
address a specific scenario where discretion was applied.

Additionally, since the replacement has already been communicated and
offered to the customer, it would not be appropriate to retract or revise
the commitment at this stage. I request the team to kindly proceed with
fulfilling the replacement as planned.


Abhishek Kumar
Cx – Escalation || Team – CEO

“Customer experience is the heart of everything we do.”

emails.body:
Hi Maheswari,

Find the RCA below.

*Observation:*

On 14th June 2025, store LKST111 placed an order for the customer with 1
John Jacobs frame along with BLU Screen Normal Corridor Progressive lenses
with Photochromatic BLU coating. The order was delivered on 18th June 2025.

On 27th December 2025, the customer visited the same store reporting that
his mother was facing difficulty seeing indoors, as the lenses remained
dark and tinted even indoors, which should not have been the case.

The issue was noticed within two weeks of delivery, however the customer’s
mother was managing initially, but discomfort increased over time.

The store checked the glasses and acknowledged the issue.

A return approval under warranty claim was raised by the store and approved
by the Need Approval team member Rishabh Sharma.

The store placed an exchange order (Order ID 1328392101) on 7th January
2026, which was later cancelled, and store credit worth ₹8,000 was released.

The customer requested a refund, which was denied as it was not covered
under the refund policy.

On 8th January, the customer visited the store again for lens replacement
and submitted two frames under Order ID 1328436844, out of which one was a
branded Tory Burch frame worth ₹15,000.

On 11th January 2026, when the frames were received back at the store after
processing, the customer noticed that the Tory Burch frame was damaged,
with visible scratches. The store staff acknowledged the damage upon
inspection.

On the same day (11th January), the customer escalated the matter to the
CEO.

Gaps :

*Product Quality:* Order ID 1312206730 had photochromatic coating, however
the lenses remained dark and tinted even indoors, indicating improper
functioning, which should not have occurred.

*Local Fitting: *Under Order ID 1328436844, the branded Tory Burch frame
was damaged during the local fitting/lens replacement process, with visible
scratches and peeling of coating, indicating handling lapse by the local
fitting team.



*Regards,*
*Suraj Verma*

*Team - CEO Escalation *[image: 87Hq.gif]

emails.snippet: Hey Himanshu, I understand we're aiming to delight customers with better service, but I'd like to request a second look at our approach. Why do we offer free replacements for wear-and-tear? It
emails.body:
Hey Himanshu,

I understand we're aiming to delight customers with better service, but I'd
like to request a second look at our approach.
Why do we offer free replacements for wear-and-tear? It doesn't seem fair
to those who've been asked to pay for their replacement pairs.

How does this align with our exchange and return policy? Customers can just
write in and claim a free pair? There are other ways to show we care, like
offering a goodwill discount on frame replacements.

Supporting the store team by backing their decisions to reject free
replacements for breakages shows we value customers and staff.

Regards,
Elaine

>> Dear Peyush Sir,
>>
>> I have always admired your journey and leadership in building Lenskart,
>> and as a young professional, you have genuinely been a source of
>> inspiration for me.
>>
>> I hope this message reaches you in good health.
>>
>> I am writing this not as a complaint, but as a sincere piece of feedback
>> from a young customer who truly wanted to trust the Lenskart brand.
>>
>> In December 2025, I purchased a pair of photochromatic spectacles worth
>> ₹8,199 for my mother after saving up as a 23-year-old fresher.
>> Unfortunately, the lenses were faulty — they appeared dark even indoors.
>> What followed was nearly two weeks of repeated store visits, during which
>> my mother and I had to repeatedly convince the store staff that there was a
>> genuine issue. Eventually, the fault was acknowledged and I was issued
>> store credit of ₹8,199 instead of a refund.
>>
>> Wanting to move forward positively, I again chose to trust Lenskart. I
>> purchased a new Tory Burch frame worth ₹15,000 for my mother and requested
>> the team to utilize ₹4,000 from my existing store credit to fit lenses for
>> this frame.
>>
>> On *11 January 2026 at around 8 PM*, I visited the *Model Town, Delhi
>> store (110009)* to collect the spectacles. To my shock, the frame was
>> returned to me in a visibly damaged condition — scratched and peeling —
>> something that was immediately noticeable even to the store staff.
>>
>> When I raised this concern, a staff member named *Saurabh* responded
>> rudely and informed me that the *maximum*resolution possible was *₹5,000
>> in store credit*. At this point, I was left disheartened. A ₹15,000
>> branded frame was damaged under Lenskart’s custody, and I was being asked
>> to once again accept partial store credit and continue trusting the same
>> system.
>>
>> As someone who has already stretched himself financially — and who made
>> these purchases purely for his mother — this was extremely difficult. It
>> was not about the money alone, but about fairness, dignity, and trust.
>>
>> I truly believe Lenskart stands for customer-first values, and that is
>> why I am reaching out to you personally. I am confident this experience
>> does not reflect the standards you envision for the brand.
>>
>> For your reference:
>> *Order Number:* #1328436844
>> *Store:* Model Town, Delhi – 110009
>> *Date of Incident:* 11 January 2026
>>
>> I have attached all relevant documents for your review.
>>
>> I would genuinely appreciate a fair resolution and guidance from your
>> office. My intent is not confrontation, but closure — and to be able to
>> continue believing in Lenskart the way I once did.
>>
>> Thank you for taking the time to read this.
>>
>>
>>
>> Regards,
>>
>> Shaurya Vaid
>>

emails.body:
Hi Maheswari,

Please find the RCA for this case.

Observation:

   -

   The customer initially reached out to us in June ’25 under Case ID
   #106286424, reporting a screw fall and broken hinge issue for Order ID
   1287538529 (PID: 210558), which was purchased in May ’24.
   -

   Although the product was out of warranty, we extended support on an
   exceptional basis and provided a replacement order on 9th July ’25 under
   Order ID 1314040851 (PID: 215328).
   -

   In October ’25, the customer contacted us again, stating that the
   replacement product also had a similar screw issue. He further escalated
   the concern to the CEO Desk on 3rd Oct ’25 under Case ID #111204311,
   wherein Ankit connected with the customer and resolved the issue by fixing
   the screw.
   -

   The customer has now once again reached the CEO Desk on 24th Jan ’26
   under Case ID 116418890, stating that the frame is facing the same issue
   again, and mentioned that he has already taken delivery of the product.

------------------------------

Store Observation:

   -

   On 14th Jan ’26, the customer visited Bardhaman_G.T Road store for
   repair. The store manager physically inspected the product and observed
   that due to physical damage, the hinge was bent, causing the screw junction
   to loosen.
   -

   The product was retained at the store and sent to the LF Lab for repair.
   However, the team failed to create a QMS entry with images, due to which
   supporting documentation is unavailable. The frame was fully repaired at
   the LF Lab and received back at the store around 18th Jan ’26, after which
   the customer was informed.
   -

   On 24th Jan ’26, the customer visited the store and collected the
   repaired product, and immediately escalated the matter to the CEO Desk.


Note : The customer has shown a recurring pattern of escalating concerns
directly to the CEO Desk for every issue. Additionally, while collecting
the product, he reportedly mentioned to the store manager:

“Abhi main ek email CEO ko karunga aur aap mujhe replacement doge.”


*Action Taken : *

We tried connecting with the customer from last 3 days but he did not
responding on the call, he is keep rejecting the call. Also not sharing the
information about the email.

Once, we establish the conversation with him, will share the update on
action taken.

emails.body:
Dear Sir,

   Please find below answers for your questions.

*1. Why was the customer's age recorded as 40? What are the differences in
the procedure for a person aged 30 and a person aged 40?*

Ans: We record each customer's details in the QMS system, for which we ask
them for their date of birth. We recorded the age they stated at that time.
And there is no difference in the process for a person aged 30 years and a
person aged 40 years. We follow all the steps for everyone.

*2. In the reading test, did the customer achieve 6/6 vision with or
without glasses?*

Ans: In the reading test, the customer achieved 6/6 vision without glasses.

*3. Was this test conducted via remote eye testing or by an optometrist in
the store?*

Ans: This test was conducted by an optometrist in the store.

*What steps will we take to ensure that such errors do not happen again?*

Ans: We conduct eye examinations strictly according to company rules and
the 12-step procedure, but we will take precautions to prevent such
problems from recurring in the future.


Thanks & Regards,
Dhammpal
SM - ST608
9763778873

emails.body:
Hi Jarrod,

Please refer to the image attached below for Warranty and Exchange
Guidelines (Frame) :
[image: image.png]

Stores will primarily determine is through a visual assessment where they
access whether the break is
1. Clean snap / Rough or Jagged Snap (A clean snap indicates a
manufacturing defect)
2. Frame Alignment (To see if one side is bent to suggest force applied)
3. Inspection of surrounding breakage area (Whitening/Stretch marks
indicates some form of force applied)
4. Comparison of Left/Right hinge : If both sides present the same issue
(For e.g Loose Hinges even with tightening), it indicates a manufacturing
defect.

For exchanges with relation to frame or lenses, they will be further
assessed by either an Optician or an Optometrist. For this case, it will
help if the customer is able to provide a picture of the hinge damage for
further assessment since the store usually does not take pictures for every
exchange enquiry they receive. (We can integrate this process with the
repair flow in the future).

+Elaine <tan.yun@lenskart.sg> Please elaborate on the hinge damage on why
it does not fall under a manufacturing defect or get the Optician that was
handling this case to elaborate further. Thank you.

emails.snippet: Dear Nitin, Hope you are doing well. We would like to bring to your attention two critical issues that are currently impacting customer connectivity and successful order fulfillment at the store level.
emails.body:
Dear Nitin,

Hope you are doing well.

We would like to bring to your attention two critical issues that are
currently impacting customer connectivity and successful order fulfillment
at the store level.

*1. Store Landline Calls Marked as Spam*
All outgoing calls being made from the POS store landline are getting
flagged as *“Spam”* on customers’ phones. As a result, customers are either
not answering the calls or the calls are not getting connected at all,
assuming them to be spam.

This is severely impacting:

   -

   Customer communication
   -

   Timely case resolution
   -

   Overall customer experience

We request you to please check:

   -

   Why the store landline number is being flagged as spam
   -

   Whether this is a system-level or telecom-related issue
   -

   The process to get the number *whitelisted or corrected* to prevent spam
   tagging going forward
   [image: image.png]

*2. OTP Issue in Local Fitting – Home Delivery Orders*
In cases of *local fitting orders where customers opt for home delivery*,
customers are *not receiving OTPs*. Due to the absence of OTP
authentication:

   -

   Courier partners are unable to complete the delivery
   -

   Orders are being returned back to the store
   -

   This is leading to avoidable delays and customer dissatisfaction

Kindly investigate this issue as well and advise on the corrective steps
required to ensure OTPs are triggered correctly for such deliveries.

We request you to please treat both the above issues as *high priority*, as
they are directly impacting customer experience and operational efficiency.

*Regards,*
*Suraj Verma*

*Team - CEO Escalation *[image: 87Hq.gif]

below-mentioned order was *not delivered to the customer’s home address*,
despite *home delivery being explicitly selected at the time of order

personally visited the store*.

and requires a detailed explanation.

emails.snippet: Observation : The customer placed an order on 17th Dec'25 under Order ID 1326486085, which included two products: One powered sunglass, [PID : 134953] and One non-powered sunglass [PID 238921]: .
emails.body:
Observation :
The customer placed an order on 17th Dec’25 under Order ID 1326486085,
which included two products:
One powered sunglass, [PID : 134953] and
One non-powered sunglass [PID 238921]: .
The non-powered sunglass was scheduled for delivery on 18th Dec’25 and
powered was assigned for 22nd Dec’25, while the powered sunglass was
dispatched via Purpledrone courier under AWB: PRD010323748P and was
successfully delivered to the customer on 18th Dec’25. However, the
non-powered sunglass order was not synced in NexS, due to which it did not
move to the production stage.
On 18th Dec '25 evening, when the customer did not receive the non-powered
sunglasses, he initiated a chat under Chat ID 114690509, selecting the
undelivered product. The chatbot repeatedly responded with the message: “We
expect to get it delivered to you by 18-Dec-2025,” despite the order not
being dispatched. The bot should have either raised a delayed-dispatch
ticket or routed the chat to a live advisor, which did not happen.
On 19th Dec '25, the customer continued the chat, and the bot again
responded with the same message: “Thank you for ordering Green Brown
Transparent Full Rim Rectangle John Jacobs Stranger Things. We expect to
get it delivered to you by 18-Dec-2025.” The customer then requested to
speak with an agent and was connected to Shweta. The customer explained
that the order was scheduled for 18th Dec '25 but was still stuck in
“Preparing for Dispatch.” Shweta informed the customer that she was raising
a complaint and that the next update would be shared within 48 hours (by
21st Dec’25). The chat was closed, and although she raised a ticket for
Delay in Dispatch, the system created a closed ticket (ID: 114710349).
On 19th Dec’25 at 12:19 AM, the customer also sent an email to Email
Support under Case ID #114705067. However, the case was not assigned to any
advisor, and no response was provided. The customer followed up again via
email later that evening but still did not receive any update.
On 20th Dec’25, the customer initiated another chat under Chat ID
114752168, where the bot once again responded incorrectly: “Apologies, your
order 1326486085 for Green Brown Transparent Full Rim Rectangle John Jacobs
Stranger Things is slightly delayed. Your new estimated delivery is
18-Dec-2025.” The customer was then connected to Kirti Baghel, who informed
him that the order was not synced due to a technical issue and that it
would be synced by 21st Dec’25. She raised a ticket with WRG under Ticket
ID 114753913.
The customer requested immediate assistance and asked if the product could
be arranged from the store, as it was available there. Kirti called the
customer and explained that syncing would take approximately 24 hours. When
the customer insisted on delivery by 21st Dec’25 or store pickup, she
attempted to transfer the call to L2 support; however, the transfer failed.
After a hold of approximately 6 minutes, she resumed the call and
transferred the chat to Supervisor Sakshi Rawat.
During the chat with the supervisor, the customer added our CEO’s to Email
Case ID #114705067, converting it into a CEO Escalation. Initially, Sakshi
reiterated that the customer would need to wait until 21st Dec’25 for the
order to sync. Subsequently, she called the customer to request patience;
however, the customer insisted on receiving the product by 21st Dec’25.
Sakshi requested some time to check internally and called the customer back
after 15–20 minutes, offering to place a new order. The customer agreed and
shared the OTP for account login; however, the call got disconnected.
Sakshi immediately called the customer again and successfully placed a new
order under Order ID 1326717870. She also informed the customer that once
the earlier non-synced order gets synced, the non-powered sunglass will be
cancelled, and the amount will be credited to the customer’s store credit
and we will delete it, after which the order would be closed.

emails.body:
Dear Nitin,


Please refer to the gap mentioned below that was witnessed while preparing
the RCA for this particular escalation.


   - Tech: Order ID 1327064312
   -

   The customer updated the powers on 24th Dec’25 for two products;
   however, the Owndays frame did not sync in the system till 8th Jan’26.
   The customer also received an incorrect EDD of 31st Dec’26 via WhatsApp.
   Even after dispatch, the customer continued to receive SMS notifications
   stating that powers were pending update. Additionally, when the EDD of
   12th Jan’26 was breached, it was not revised to the next available date.


I'd request you to please help in validating the aforementioned pointers
and help us with the RCA on this.
[image: image.png]
[image: image.png]

Regards,

Himanshu | M : +91-8287561668

emails.snippet: Hi Maheswari, Please find the RCA for this case: Case Observations and Timeline of Events: Note: The customer had previously contacted us in October and November for different concerns, which were
emails.body:
Hi Maheswari,

Please find the RCA for this case:

Case Observations and Timeline of Events:

Note: The customer had previously contacted us in October and November for
different concerns, which were addressed by the team at the respective
times.

27 Oct 2025:

   -

   The customer escalated to Peyush (112306202) regarding delayed delivery
   of Order ID 1321849626.
   -

   Delivery was arranged; however, post-delivery, the customer reported
   fitting and alignment issues, stating the frame slipped while worn.
   -

   She declined to share images, mentioning the issue would not be visible
   in photos.
   -

   The order was subsequently returned and fully refunded.

8 Nov 2025:

   -

   The customer again wrote to Peyush (112306202) regarding Order ID
   1315274660, placed on 25 Jul 2025 under the Buy 2nd Later option.
   -

   She placed the second order 1317733435 on 27 Aug 2025 using the Buy 2nd
   Later voucher for a JJ frame (130333, Medium – 134 mm).
   -

   The order was returned due to fitting issues, and the refund was
   processed; however, the voucher was not received back.
   -

   The concern was raised regarding non-receipt of the voucher post return.

Resolution:

   -

   Advisor Abhishek created and shared a ₹1,500 voucher with the customer.

16 Nov 2025:

   -

   The customer placed Order ID 1324048725 for a Hustlr frame (224173 –
   Narrow, 132 mm) using the voucher and paid an additional ₹1,000.
   -

   The order was delivered on 21 Nov 2025.

24 Nov 2025:

   -

   The customer reported alignment issues via email (113607549), stating
   the store attempted repairs but could not resolve the issue.
   -

   She requested a replacement before submitting the existing frame, as she
   did not have a spare product.
   -

   Advisor Sahil contacted the customer and raised Ticket #113610732.
   -

   ₹1,000 store credits were added by Khusi Sidana on the same day as an
   exception, prior to return.

26 Nov 2025:

   -

   The customer replied by email stating she received only ₹1,000 in store
   credits and requested the remaining amount to place a new order.

27–28 Nov 2025:

   -

   The ticket 113610732 remained unassigned on 27 Nov and was assigned to
   Aparna on 28 Nov, with no initial action taken.

29 Nov 2025:

   -

   Aparna contacted the customer, shared voucher details for the remaining
   amount, and closed the ticket.
   -

   Later the same day, the customer reported being at the store and facing
   issues while using the voucher.

At 3:25 PM:

   -

   The customer placed Order ID 1325065016 at Gurgaon_Sapphire 90 (PID:
   234501 – Wide, 138 mm) using the store credits and voucher.
   -

   The store requested the KMT team to ensure enhanced QC.
   -

   The order was inadvertently placed under the Buy 2nd Later option,
   resulting in a voucher being issued post-delivery.


At 4:46 PM:

   -

   Advisor Kritika attempted to contact the customer; the call
   disconnected. Upon verification, it was found that the voucher had already
   been used and a new order was placed. Order details were shared, and the
   ticket was closed.
   -

   Upon delivery, the customer returned her old frame to the store.
   -

   We connected with the store team and as per them, minor alignment issues
   were identified and fixed; however, the customer remained dissatisfied and
   opted for a replacement.

10 Jan 2026:

   -

   The customer wrote to Peyush again (115776959), stating that the Buy 2nd
   Later voucher received against Order ID 1325065016 had expired as she was
   out of town. She also reported recurring alignment issues with the current
   frame.
   -

   When requested to share images, she declined, stating the issue would
   not be captured. When advised to visit the store, she stated she had the
   store details and would visit at her convenience.

16th Jan 2026

   -

   The customer again wrote to Peyush, reporting that the alignment issue
   persisted and that the nose pad had also come off, further adding to her
   frustration.
   -

   She was requested to share images of the issue; however, the images have
   not been received so far.



*Note: *The customer seems confused about the product size and fitting
issues. We observed that in all the orders placed, the customer placed the
order for a different frame size.

   1.

      Order 1317733435: It was placed for JJ frame (130333, Medium – 134
      mm).
      2.

      Order 1324048725: It was placed for Hustlr frame (224173 – Narrow,
      132 mm)
      3.

      Order 1325065016: It was placed for VC (PID: 234501 – Wide, 138 mm.


Action Taken

   -

   Contacted the customer to acknowledge the concern and apologized for the
   inconvenience caused.
   -

   Clarified that the order against which the Buy 2nd Later voucher was
   generated was originally intended for a single product only.
   -

   Considering the situation and customer experience, a new voucher was
   issued as a one-time exception.
   -

   Requested images of the product to assess the reported issues; however,
   the customer declined, stating the problem would not be visible in images
   and images are yet to be received.
   -

   The customer informed that she would visit the store for inspection or
   replacement but did not share a specific date or time.
   -

   The store team was proactively informed about the customer’s potential
   visit and instructed to extend full support.
   -

   Prior to visiting the store, the customer reached out again stating that
   the nose pad had come off and that she was encountering errors while using
   the voucher.
   -

   New order placed 1329195304 using the voucher and monitoring it until
   the delivery.

emails.body:
Hi,

16 year olds come under the kid category and classical case of
accommodation and nullifying the astigmatism in AR.
Also the previous power did not have a Cylinder value.
Ideal process -  Take 5 readings of AR and check for the inconsistency >1D
within each reading.
These are to be done by ASCO certified optometrist only.

*RCA *- Optometrist Ranju was not certified and was not allowed to do kids
eye test.
*Preventive action* - Kids eye test training undergoing 15th to 21st Jan
for 4900 store optometrists where these cases would be early identified.

Kindly let me know if you have any specific questions related to this
case.


Regards,
Japin

emails.snippet: Hey Nitin, 1. Chatbot relies on order status in cosmos and EDD in Juno. There is no mechanism to use nexs status to update EDD. 2. A feature to update EDD of all orders whose EDD has passed went live
emails.body:
Hey Nitin,

1. Chatbot relies on order status in cosmos and EDD in Juno. There is no
mechanism to use nexs status to update EDD.
2. A feature to update EDD of all orders whose EDD has passed went live on
Friday (Jan 9). Any other safeguards to ensure EDD is accurate will need to
be built elsewhere, not in chatbot.
3. We had built a feature to route such cases to human agents but due to
the high volume we had rolled it back. We will implement a feature where if
the customer mentions delay a couple times while requesting agent connect,
we will provide this connect.

>
> Hi Maheswari,
> Please see if this customer can be helped to resolve this issue
>

> Arpit Upadhyay
> CEO’s Office | Lenskart

> ---------- Forwarded message ---------
> From: Shaurya Vaid <shaurya3602@gmail.com>
> Date: Sun, 11 Jan 2026 at 8:55 PM
> Subject: When Trust Costs ₹15,000: A Loyal Customer’s Honest Experience
> To: peyush.bansal@lenskart.com <peyush.bansal@lenskart.com>
> Cc: <arpit.upadhyay@lenskart.com>, Puja Vaid <puja.vaid1@gmail.com>,
> Ashwani Vaid <ashwani22@yahoo.com>
>
>
> Dear Peyush Sir,
>
> I have always admired your journey and leadership in building Lenskart,
> and as a young professional, you have genuinely been a source of
> inspiration for me.
>
> I hope this message reaches you in good health.
>
> I am writing this not as a complaint, but as a sincere piece of feedback
> from a young customer who truly wanted to trust the Lenskart brand.
>
> In December 2025, I purchased a pair of photochromatic spectacles worth
> ₹8,199 for my mother after saving up as a 23-year-old fresher.
> Unfortunately, the lenses were faulty — they appeared dark even indoors.
> What followed was nearly two weeks of repeated store visits, during which
> my mother and I had to repeatedly convince the store staff that there was a
> genuine issue. Eventually, the fault was acknowledged and I was issued
> store credit of ₹8,199 instead of a refund.
>
> Wanting to move forward positively, I again chose to trust Lenskart. I
> purchased a new Tory Burch frame worth ₹15,000 for my mother and requested
> the team to utilize ₹4,000 from my existing store credit to fit lenses for
> this frame.
>
> On *11 January 2026 at around 8 PM*, I visited the *Model Town, Delhi
> store (110009)* to collect the spectacles. To my shock, the frame was
> returned to me in a visibly damaged condition — scratched and peeling —
> something that was immediately noticeable even to the store staff.
>
> When I raised this concern, a staff member named *Saurabh* responded
> rudely and informed me that the *maximum*resolution possible was *₹5,000
> in store credit*. At this point, I was left disheartened. A ₹15,000
> branded frame was damaged under Lenskart’s custody, and I was being asked
> to once again accept partial store credit and continue trusting the same
> system.
>
> As someone who has already stretched himself financially — and who made
> these purchases purely for his mother — this was extremely difficult. It
> was not about the money alone, but about fairness, dignity, and trust.
>
> I truly believe Lenskart stands for customer-first values, and that is why
> I am reaching out to you personally. I am confident this experience does
> not reflect the standards you envision for the brand.
>
> For your reference:
> *Order Number:* #1328436844
> *Store:* Model Town, Delhi – 110009
> *Date of Incident:* 11 January 2026
>
> I have attached all relevant documents for your review.
>
> I would genuinely appreciate a fair resolution and guidance from your
> office. My intent is not confrontation, but closure — and to be able to
> continue believing in Lenskart the way I once did.
>
> Thank you for taking the time to read this.
>
>
>
> Regards,
>
> Shaurya Vaid
>

Date: Sun, 11 Jan 2026 at 8:55 PM
Subject: When Trust Costs ₹15,000: A Loyal Customer’s Honest Experience
To: peyush.bansal@lenskart.com <peyush.bansal@lenskart.com>
Cc: <arpit.upadhyay@lenskart.com>, Puja Vaid <puja.vaid1@gmail.com>,
Ashwani Vaid <ashwani22@yahoo.com>


Dear Peyush Sir,

I have always admired your journey and leadership in building Lenskart, and
as a young professional, you have genuinely been a source of inspiration
for me.

I hope this message reaches you in good health.

I am writing this not as a complaint, but as a sincere piece of feedback
from a young customer who truly wanted to trust the Lenskart brand.

In December 2025, I purchased a pair of photochromatic spectacles worth
₹8,199 for my mother after saving up as a 23-year-old fresher.
Unfortunately, the lenses were faulty — they appeared dark even indoors.
What followed was nearly two weeks of repeated store visits, during which
my mother and I had to repeatedly convince the store staff that there was a
genuine issue. Eventually, the fault was acknowledged and I was issued
store credit of ₹8,199 instead of a refund.

Wanting to move forward positively, I again chose to trust Lenskart. I
purchased a new Tory Burch frame worth ₹15,000 for my mother and requested
the team to utilize ₹4,000 from my existing store credit to fit lenses for
this frame.

On *11 January 2026 at around 8 PM*, I visited the *Model Town, Delhi store
(110009)* to collect the spectacles. To my shock, the frame was returned to
me in a visibly damaged condition — scratched and peeling — something that
was immediately noticeable even to the store staff.

When I raised this concern, a staff member named *Saurabh* responded rudely
and informed me that the *maximum*resolution possible was *₹5,000 in store
credit*. At this point, I was left disheartened. A ₹15,000 branded frame
was damaged under Lenskart’s custody, and I was being asked to once again
accept partial store credit and continue trusting the same system.

As someone who has already stretched himself financially — and who made
these purchases purely for his mother — this was extremely difficult. It
was not about the money alone, but about fairness, dignity, and trust.

I truly believe Lenskart stands for customer-first values, and that is why
I am reaching out to you personally. I am confident this experience does
not reflect the standards you envision for the brand.

For your reference:
*Order Number:* #1328436844
*Store:* Model Town, Delhi – 110009
*Date of Incident:* 11 January 2026

I have attached all relevant documents for your review.

I would genuinely appreciate a fair resolution and guidance from your
office. My intent is not confrontation, but closure — and to be able to
continue believing in Lenskart the way I once did.

Thank you for taking the time to read this.



Regards,

Shaurya Vaid

Hi All,



This escalation stands closed. Even though our system failed to send a CSAT
survey due to an ongoing glitch, I believe there's no better metric/tool to
measure a happy customer than to see this smile on this customer’s face.



Honestly, that's worth way more than a perfect score :)



*Sharing customer's heartfelt appreciation towards the assistance he
received - *

Hi Peyush,

I am writing this email to express my sincere gratitude for the time, care,
and effort you and your team invested in investigating the issue. In a
world where it’s easy to move on quickly, the fact that you chose to pause,
listen, and act with intent truly meant a lot to us.

A very special thanks to Dipak for his patience, empathy, and for genuinely
listening to the facts without judgment. His calm approach and commitment
to restoring trust made a difficult experience feel humane and reassuring.
What touched me the most, was the way my son, Spandan, was made happy. For
a child to feel acknowledged and valued is incredibly powerful and it left
a lasting impression on him.

In his own words, he wanted me to share this with you:

*“Thank you Peyush uncle and Dipak uncle — thank you very much. I loved the
milk mug very, very much and off course the chocolates. Peyush uncle, you
are my favourite Shark. Someday, I would want to meet you too.”*

As a parent, seeing that smile and hearing those words made everything
worthwhile. Moments like these build trust not just in a brand, but in the
people behind it.

Thank you once again for leading with empathy and setting such a strong
example. It truly makes a difference.

Warm regards,
M S Roy
(on behalf of Spandan)

To: Maheswari M <maheswari.m@lenskart.com>

himanshu.gupta2@lenskart.in>



Hi Maheswari,



Please find the detailed RCA for this case:



*Customer Name:* Spandan Singha Roy

*Order ID:* 1327625765

*Order placement Date:* 30th Dec 2025 4:09 PM

*Sale Source: *Lenskart Store (Kamarhati_Kolkata)

*Customer category and MVC score:* Silver+/No



*Products:*

   - Lens Only (bluecut_1.6)



*Issue Reported:*

   - Wrong sales practice at the store.
   - Delayed in home delivery.



*Case Observations*

   - On 30th Dec 2025 at 4:09 PM, the customer visited the Kamarhati_Kolkata
   store (LKST975) to place an order for his son.
   - The customer intended to purchase only a single powered eyeglass.
   - The store manager Debasis Das personally attended the customer and
   assisted with order placement.
   - As per the store, the customer selected PID 209501 with Owndays
   Lenskart BLU+ lens package, where the total cart value was above 2k.
   - At the time of billing, the store team attempted to apply the SINGLE
   voucher; however, the voucher could not be applied due to a system error
   stating that it was not applicable to the cart.
   - Since the voucher could not be applied and full payment was required,
   the store team offered the BOGO and BOGOGO option, which the customer
   declined as he wanted to purchase only one product.
   - As an alternative, the store team informed the customer about a free
   lens cleaner voucher and helped him in purchasing the voucher online using
   his mobile phone under Order ID 1327624456.
   - Subsequently, using the same voucher, the store team placed a
   lens-only order (Order ID 1327625765) for his son using his old frame with
   the lens bluecut_1.6.
   - After returning home, the customer attempted to place an order
   independently and found that he was able to place a single kids’ eyewear
   order online.
   - While doing so, he selected a similar but different product (PID
   222805 – Sale PID) with an Anti-Glare lens package (Free), and the total
   cart value came to ₹649.
   - Based on this, the customer assumed that the store team had
   incorrectly denied the single-product purchase and also charged him more,
   which he perceived as an incorrect sales practice.
   - On 1st Jan at 10:20 AM, the order was received at the store, and a
   newly joined staff member Shoyeb Aktar Sk accepted the order. However,
   he missed assigning a courier for the home delivery, despite it being a
   ship-to-customer order.
   - As a result, the order remained at the store until 6th Jan.



*CS Touchpoints*

*Conversation with Deepak Dhami (Sales Team)*

*On 5th Jan 2026*

   - At 9:46 PM, the customer attempted to connect with a support agent via
   chat #115552921; however, he was initially presented only with automated
   BOT options for order tracking. The absence of an immediate human
   interaction made it difficult for the customer to connect with Customer
   Support.
   - However, just after 4 minutes at 9:50 PM, the customer connected with
   Deepak Dhami on chat via the same chat regarding the delay in delivery and
   also highlighted his in-store experience, reporting that the store denied
   the option of purchasing a single powered eyeglass for a child. The chat
   was handled by Deepak Dhami.
   - Deepak informed the customer that the order had been shipped, however,
   the exact and accurate delivery status was not shared. He also communicated
   that the chat would be transferred to the Customer Support team and the
   team will assist during operational hours (10:00 AM – 9:00 PM the next day)
   with your concern. The customer was not satisfied.
   - During the same conversation, the customer asked to clarify his doubt,
   “Let me know if a single kids’ powered order can be placed?” Deepak
   misinterpreted this query as an intent to place a new order and responded
   that he could assist in placing the order.
   - Subsequently, the customer also shared power details, which further
   reinforced the advisor’s assumption that the customer wished to place a new
   order. However, the conversation later went non-responsive. This
   interaction contributed to the customer’s perception of being upsold,
   further impacting his overall experience.



*Conversation with Harsh Gupta*

   - On 6th Jan at 7:58 PM, the customer continued the same chat #115552921
   and connected with Harsh Gupta.
   - Harsh informed the customer that the order had been delivered to the
   store but did not initially verify that it was a ship-to-customer order,
   and mistakenly asked the customer to collect it from the store.
   - Upon correction, Harsh raised a ticket 115600527 to the offline team
   to arrange home delivery and shared a tentative timeline of 8th Jan.
   - The customer remained dissatisfied with the timeline and requested
   Peyush’s email ID for escalation.
   - Harsh connected with the store team (115600970) and requested urgent
   delivery. The store team confirmed courier assignment; however, Harsh
   requested manual home delivery by store staff, which was agreed upon,
   subject to manpower availability.
   - He also attempted to connect with the store manager (115601328) to
   understand the alleged denial of a single kids’ eyewear purchase, but the
   call went unanswered.
   - He later informed the customer that delivery would be arranged by 4:00
   PM next day, which the customer disagreed with, stating that the store was
   only 10–15 minutes away and requested delivery by 11:00 AM.
   - The customer questioned why the order was delivered to the store
   despite providing a home address and without OTP confirmation.
   - Despite explanations, the customer remained dissatisfied and again
   threatened escalation.



*Supervisor Intervention*

   - Since the customer threatened to escalate the matter, Harsh arranged a
   callback from the supervisor.
   - At 9:16 PM, Supervisor Shaquib connected with the customer
   (#115552921), coordinated with the store, and assured delivery within 30
   minutes, which was successfully completed.
   - During the call, the customer reiterated concerns regarding store
   experience and sales practices. Shaquib requested time to investigate and
   share an update.



*CEO Escalation:*

   - During the same conversation, the customer escalated the matter to
   Peyush via email (#115602496) expressing dissatisfaction with both the
   store experience and delivery handling.



*Action Taken:*

   1. We contacted the customer, acknowledged his concerns, and apologized
   sincerely for the inconvenience caused.
   2. We clarified that the frame and lens package selected at the store
   differed from the one chosen later on the application, which resulted in a
   significant price difference.
   3. We explained that the store team attempted to place the order for a
   single product, and therefore shared the cart value above 2k based on the
   product selection. Had the order not been feasible, the store would have
   declined it at the initial stage without quoting a price.
   4. We informed the customer that since the voucher could not be applied
   due to a system error, the store team suggested the BOGO and BOGOGO option
   so that the customer could receive maximum value at the same price point,
   and not to upsell.
   5. We assured improved communication and handling going forward, both at
   the store and Customer Support levels.
   6. Considering the overall dissatisfaction and the delay in the order
   for his son, we offered a frame free of cost (FOC) as a goodwill gesture to
   resolve the concern empathetically.



*Also, sharing the pointers for the question asked by Peyush sir:*



*1. Difficulty connecting with CS via App*

   - The customer connected around 10:00 PM, when the CS team was
   unavailable. He was seeking immediate human assistance on chat but was
   initially connected to the BOT, which provided order-related automated
   options and the customer felt it’s difficult to connect with a human agent.

*2. Online–Offline Gap*

   - While placing the order on the app, the customer selected a similar
   but different Sale PID (222805) with a different lens package, resulting in
   a lower cart value. This led him to assume that the store team had
   overcharged him. However, there was no Gap in pricing.

*3. Upselling by CS*

   - There was no intentional upselling by the CS team. The initial
   interaction was with a sales agent, who misunderstood the customer’s query
   as an intent to place a new order and offered assistance accordingly, which
   was perceived by the customer as upselling.



Currently, waiting for the response from Store Leadership to understand if
the store manager really denied a single eyewear purchase for kids.

persuaded to instead opt for a lens change in the old frame, buying some

found that the exact frame my son liked (which is currently in my account

ensure such experiences are not repeated for any customer in the future.
