emails.body:
Hi All,

This escalation stands closed. Even though our system failed to send a CSAT
survey due to an ongoing glitch, I believe there's no better metric/tool to
measure a happy customer than to see this smile on this customer’s face.

Honestly, that's worth way more than a perfect score :)

*Sharing customer's heartfelt appreciation towards the assistance he
received - *

Hi Peyush,

I am writing this email to express my sincere gratitude for the time, care,
and effort you and your team invested in investigating the issue. In a
world where it’s easy to move on quickly, the fact that you chose to pause,
listen, and act with intent truly meant a lot to us.

A very special thanks to Dipak for his patience, empathy, and for genuinely
listening to the facts without judgment. His calm approach and commitment
to restoring trust made a difficult experience feel humane and reassuring.
What touched me the most, was the way my son, Spandan, was made happy. For
a child to feel acknowledged and valued is incredibly powerful and it left
a lasting impression on him.

In his own words, he wanted me to share this with you:

*“Thank you Peyush uncle and Dipak uncle — thank you very much. I loved the
milk mug very, very much and off course the chocolates. Peyush uncle, you
are my favourite Shark. Someday, I would want to meet you too.”*

[image: PastedGraphic-1.png]

As a parent, seeing that smile and hearing those words made everything
worthwhile. Moments like these build trust not just in a brand, but in the
people behind it.

Thank you once again for leading with empathy and setting such a strong
example. It truly makes a difference.

Warm regards,
M S Roy
(on behalf of Spandan)

emails.snippet: Hi Maheswari, Please find the detailed RCA for this case: Customer Name: Spandan Singha Roy Order ID: 1327625765 Order placement Date: 30th Dec 2025 4:09 PM Sale Source: Lenskart Store (
emails.body:
Hi Maheswari,

Please find the detailed RCA for this case:

Customer Name: Spandan Singha Roy

Order ID: 1327625765

Order placement Date: 30th Dec 2025 4:09 PM

Sale Source: Lenskart Store (Kamarhati_Kolkata)

Customer category and MVC score: Silver+/No


Products:

   -

   Lens Only (bluecut_1.6)


Issue Reported:

   -

   Wrong sales practice at the store.
   -

   Delayed in home delivery.


Case Observations

   -

   On 30th Dec 2025 at 4:09 PM, the customer visited the Kamarhati_Kolkata
   store (LKST975) to place an order for his son.
   -

   The customer intended to purchase only a single powered eyeglass.
   -

   The store manager Debasis Das personally attended the customer and
   assisted with order placement.
   -

   As per the store, the customer selected PID 209501 with Owndays Lenskart
   BLU+ lens package, where the total cart value was above 2k.
   -

   At the time of billing, the store team attempted to apply the SINGLE
   voucher; however, the voucher could not be applied due to a system error
   stating that it was not applicable to the cart.
   -

   Since the voucher could not be applied and full payment was required,
   the store team offered the BOGO and BOGOGO option, which the customer
   declined as he wanted to purchase only one product.
   -

   As an alternative, the store team informed the customer about a free
   lens cleaner voucher and helped him in purchasing the voucher online using
   his mobile phone under Order ID 1327624456.
   -

   Subsequently, using the same voucher, the store team placed a lens-only
   order (Order ID 1327625765) for his son using his old frame with the lens
   bluecut_1.6.
   -

   After returning home, the customer attempted to place an order
   independently and found that he was able to place a single kids’ eyewear
   order online.
   -

   While doing so, he selected a similar but different product (PID 222805
   – Sale PID) with an Anti-Glare lens package (Free), and the total cart
   value came to ₹649.
   -

   Based on this, the customer assumed that the store team had incorrectly
   denied the single-product purchase and also charged him more, which he
   perceived as an incorrect sales practice.
   -

   On 1st Jan at 10:20 AM, the order was received at the store, and a newly
   joined staff member Shoyeb Aktar Sk accepted the order. However, he missed
   assigning a courier for the home delivery, despite it being a
   ship-to-customer order.
   -

   As a result, the order remained at the store until 6th Jan.


CS Touchpoints

Conversation with Deepak Dhami (Sales Team)

On 5th Jan 2026

   -

   At 9:46 PM, the customer attempted to connect with a support agent via
   chat #115552921; however, he was initially presented only with automated
   BOT options for order tracking. The absence of an immediate human
   interaction made it difficult for the customer to connect with Customer
   Support.
   -

   However, just after 4 minutes at 9:50 PM, the customer connected with
   Deepak Dhami on chat via the same chat regarding the delay in delivery and
   also highlighted his in-store experience, reporting that the store denied
   the option of purchasing a single powered eyeglass for a child. The chat
   was handled by Deepak Dhami.
   -

   Deepak informed the customer that the order had been shipped, however,
   the exact and accurate delivery status was not shared. He also communicated
   that the chat would be transferred to the Customer Support team and the
   team will assist during operational hours (10:00 AM – 9:00 PM the next day)
   with your concern. The customer was not satisfied.
   -

   During the same conversation, the customer asked to clarify his doubt,
   “Let me know if a single kids’ powered order can be placed?” Deepak
   misinterpreted this query as an intent to place a new order and responded
   that he could assist in placing the order.
   -

   Subsequently, the customer also shared power details, which further
   reinforced the advisor’s assumption that the customer wished to place a new
   order. However, the conversation later went non-responsive. This
   interaction contributed to the customer’s perception of being upsold,
   further impacting his overall experience.


Conversation with Harsh Gupta

   -

   On 6th Jan at 7:58 PM, the customer continued the same chat #115552921
   and connected with Harsh Gupta.
   -

   Harsh informed the customer that the order had been delivered to the
   store but did not initially verify that it was a ship-to-customer order,
   and mistakenly asked the customer to collect it from the store.
   -

   Upon correction, Harsh raised a ticket 115600527 to the offline team to
   arrange home delivery and shared a tentative timeline of 8th Jan.
   -

   The customer remained dissatisfied with the timeline and requested
   Peyush’s email ID for escalation.
   -

   Harsh connected with the store team (115600970) and requested urgent
   delivery. The store team confirmed courier assignment; however, Harsh
   requested manual home delivery by store staff, which was agreed upon,
   subject to manpower availability.
   -

   He also attempted to connect with the store manager (115601328) to
   understand the alleged denial of a single kids’ eyewear purchase, but the
   call went unanswered.
   -

   He later informed the customer that delivery would be arranged by 4:00
   PM next day, which the customer disagreed with, stating that the store was
   only 10–15 minutes away and requested delivery by 11:00 AM.
   -

   The customer questioned why the order was delivered to the store despite
   providing a home address and without OTP confirmation.
   -

   Despite explanations, the customer remained dissatisfied and again
   threatened escalation.


Supervisor Intervention

   -

   Since the customer threatened to escalate the matter, Harsh arranged a
   callback from the supervisor.
   -

   At 9:16 PM, Supervisor Shaquib connected with the customer (#115552921),
   coordinated with the store, and assured delivery within 30 minutes, which
   was successfully completed.
   -

   During the call, the customer reiterated concerns regarding store
   experience and sales practices. Shaquib requested time to investigate and
   share an update.


CEO Escalation:

   -

   During the same conversation, the customer escalated the matter to
   Peyush via email (#115602496) expressing dissatisfaction with both the
   store experience and delivery handling.


Action Taken:

   1. We contacted the customer, acknowledged his concerns, and apologized
   sincerely for the inconvenience caused.
   2. We clarified that the frame and lens package selected at the store
   differed from the one chosen later on the application, which resulted in a
   significant price difference.
   3. We explained that the store team attempted to place the order for a
   single product, and therefore shared the cart value above 2k based on the
   product selection. Had the order not been feasible, the store would have
   declined it at the initial stage without quoting a price.
   4. We informed the customer that since the voucher could not be applied
   due to a system error, the store team suggested the BOGO and BOGOGO option
   so that the customer could receive maximum value at the same price point,
   and not to upsell.
   5. We assured improved communication and handling going forward, both at
   the store and Customer Support levels.
   6. Considering the overall dissatisfaction and the delay in the order
   for his son, we offered a frame free of cost (FOC) as a goodwill gesture to
   resolve the concern empathetically.


*Also, sharing the pointers for the question asked by Peyush sir:*


*1. Difficulty connecting with CS via App*


   - The customer connected around 10:00 PM, when the CS team was
   unavailable. He was seeking immediate human assistance on chat but was
   initially connected to the BOT, which provided order-related automated
   options and the customer felt it’s difficult to connect with a human agent.

*2. Online–Offline Gap*


   - While placing the order on the app, the customer selected a similar
   but different Sale PID (222805) with a different lens package, resulting in
   a lower cart value. This led him to assume that the store team had
   overcharged him. However, there was no Gap in pricing.

*3. Upselling by CS*


   - There was no intentional upselling by the CS team. The initial
   interaction was with a sales agent, who misunderstood the customer’s query
   as an intent to place a new order and offered assistance accordingly, which
   was perceived by the customer as upselling.


Currently, waiting for the response from Store Leadership to understand if
the store manager really denied a single eyewear purchase for kids.

emails.body:
Dear Devendra,

During a recent CEO escalation review, we observed a concern wherein *LF*
orders do not reflect the lens package name on the invoice. This creates a
clear gap in transparency and may lead to customer dissatisfaction,
especially when invoices are required for future reference or verification.

We request you to kindly review this issue on priority and ensure that the
lens package details are clearly mentioned on invoices for LF orders going
forward. Addressing this at the system level will help prevent similar
escalations and improve overall customer trust.

Hi Peyush,
I am writing this email with a sense of disappointment and concern
regarding my recent experience with your company, specifically related to
Order No. 1327625765.

During my visit to your Kamarhatti_Kolkata store, the sales representative
misinformed both me and my 12-year-old son by stating that a single
eyeglass could not be ordered for a child, and that I must either purchase
a 1+1 offer worth INR 2,600 or pay the same amount even for a single
eyeglass. Based on this information and trusting your brand, I was
persuaded to instead opt for a lens change in the old frame, buying some
coupon and paying INR 700 altogether.

However, to my utter surprise, after returning home I checked your app and
found that the exact frame my son liked (which is currently in my account
basket) was clearly available for single purchase at approximately INR 650.
This left me feeling deeply disheartened. It is painful to believe that
store staff may be taking advantage of customer trust in order to meet
sales targets. While I chose to let this incident go, assuming it to be
fate and out of sympathy for the store staff doing it to meet the Sales
metrics. However, the subsequent events have only added more to my
disappointment.

The delivery was scheduled for 5th January, but the product was not
delivered. After significant effort, I contacted customer support through
your app and connected with Mr. Deepak Dhami, who instead of resolving my
concern, attempted to sell me another eyeglass. I was informed that the
item had been dispatched and that the relevant team would contact me.
Unfortunately, no one did.
On 6th January, after yet another exhaustive follow-up, I connected with
Ms. Harsha Gupta, who informed me that the eyeglass had actually been
delivered to the Kamarhatti_Kolkata store, and that I would need to collect
it from there.

This entire experience raises some serious and concerning questions:

Is customer money not valued as real and important?
Can a business truly function without trust and transparency with its
customers?
Is there no empathy for delayed orders—especially when the product is for a
12-year-old child with an eye condition?
How was the order delivered to a store instead of my residential address,
and how was my OTP shared and accepted at the store? This raises concerns
not only about store practices but also about your last-mile delivery
process.

I am writing this not merely to complain, but with the expectation of
serious introspection, corrective action, and a clear explanation of what
went wrong. I would appreciate being informed about the steps taken to
ensure such experiences are not repeated for any customer in the future.
I have always associated your brand with trust and customer care, which
makes this experience particularly disappointing.
Looking forward to your response.

Warm regards,
M S Roy
9779493941

Dear Team,

This is in reference to a recent CEO Escalation received today, wherein the
customer has reached out to us reporting that incorrect powers were
provided, resulting in significant discomfort and inconvenience.

We have already connected with the store team at @Lkst1815 Thane_Hiranandani
<hiranandanirdhiranandani.thane@lenskartstore.com>, who informed us that
the eye test was conducted by a tele-optometrist. The store also mentioned
that similar prescription-related issues have been observed with other
customers and that this concern had earlier been highlighted to @Maheswari M
<maheswari.m@lenskart.com> in relation to a different case.

Despite replacing the lenses with the correct powers, the customer remains
extremely dissatisfied, as the issue has impacted his overall trust and
experience. Understandably, the customer is viewing this as a serious lapse
and is highly distressed due to the inconvenience caused.

Sharing the VOC for your reference to seek your guidance on how best we can
proceed further to address the customer’s concern and provide a fair
resolution in this case.

Your support and direction will help us close this escalation appropriately
and ensure corrective actions are aligned.

VOC:
Sub:Major Escalation: Incorrect Eye Test Lenskart Hiranandani Estate Branch
31 Dec 25, 11:47 AM
From:piyushchouradia09@gmail.com
Dear Mr. Peeyush Bansal and Lenskart Leadership Team,

I am writing this email as a serious and urgent escalation regarding a
highly alarming experience at a Lenskart store concerning the digital eye
check-up platform used for prescribing lenses.

During my visit to the Lenskart store, I underwent an eye test using your
in-store digital eye testing system. Based on this test, a prescription was
generated and spectacles were issued to me. However, after experiencing
discomfort and vision issues, I consulted an external qualified eye doctor,
who confirmed that the prescription provided by Lenskart was incorrect.

This is a major health and safety concern. Incorrect lens power can cause:

Eye strain and headaches

Vision deterioration

Long-term eye damage

It is extremely alarming that such incorrect prescriptions are being issued
through a platform that customers trust for their eye health. This raises
serious questions about the accuracy, calibration, and professional
validation of the digital eye testing system being used in your stores.

Because of this negligence:

I had to consult an external eye specialist at my own cost

I was given incorrect lenses that could have damaged my eyesight

My trust in the brand has been severely impacted

My Demands:

Complete refund of the full cost of my spectacles

Compensation for the inconvenience, health risk, and external doctor
consultation

A formal investigation into the eye testing system and staff training at
the concerned store

A written explanation on how such critical errors are allowed to occur

This matter is non-negotiable as it involves customer health and safety. If
this issue is not addressed promptly and satisfactorily, I will be forced
to escalate this further to consumer grievance forums and regulatory
authorities.

I expect a written response within 48 hours confirming refund and
compensation details.

Store Location: [Hiranandani Estate Thane West Mumbai
Order ID - 1325733607
Date of Visit: 7th Dec 2025

Looking forward to an immediate and responsible resolution.

Best Regards
Piyush Chouradiya

screw.

get the same size screw hence they sent the product to LF for the same size
screw fitting(as cx refused to accept a bigger screw).

Lab fitted same size screw and sent back to store, accordingly handovered
to cx. Now cx is complaining that scratches generated over the frame while
as per sm she asked cx to click the images of your frame in front of

emails.snippet: Hi Maheswari, Please find the RCA of this case below. Observation: On 25th Dec 2025, LKST907 placed an order (ID 1327223123) for a customer consisting of 4 products (1 Owndays, 2 VC, and 1 JJ sunglass)
emails.body:
Hi Maheswari,

Please find the RCA of this case below.

*Observation:*

   1.

   On *25th Dec 2025*, *LKST907* placed an order (*ID 1327223123*) for a
   customer consisting of *4 products* (1 Owndays, 2 VC, and 1 JJ
   sunglass). The order was delivered between *26th–27th Dec*.
   2.

   On *28th Dec*, *LKST2011* contacted *PRG Voice* and connected with *Advisor
   Shivaji Namdev (Case ID: 115140267)*.
   -

      The store informed that the customer wanted to return *JJ PID 134949*
      and exchange it with *Meller PID 238521*.
      -

      The advisor incorrectly stated that a *price difference would apply
      due to brand change*, despite both frames being *₹5,000 capped*.
      -

      The customer was physically present at the store and claimed she had
      been informed earlier by *LKST907* that frame exchange within the
      ₹5,000 cap was allowed.
      -

      When the store handed the call to the customer, the advisor *disconnected
      the call abruptly and did not call back*, escalating the situation at
      the store.
      3.

   The store again contacted *PRG Voice* and connected with *Advisor Komal
   Gupta (Case ID: 115140653)*.
   -

      The advisor repeated the *same incorrect information* regarding brand
      change and price difference.
      -

      The store clarified that earlier policy allowed exchange within the
      same capped value, including lens value.
      -

      The advisor stated that the policy had been updated but was *unaware
      of the correct policy*, which clearly mentions eligibility for
      exchange within the same value (including lens).
      -

      The customer became extremely frustrated, mentioned being an
      advocate, threatened legal action, and disconnected the call. No
      de-escalation or escalation was initiated by the advisor.
      4.

   On *28th Dec at 4:41 PM*, the customer attempted to initiate a return
   via the app, which was later cancelled as it did not address her concern.

            On *29th Dec 2025 at 4:30 AM*, the customer escalated the
matter directly to the *CEO*, reporting the complete experience.

*Action Taken:*

   -

   Connected with the customer, acknowledged the inconvenience, and issued
   a sincere apology.
   -

   Clarified the correct policy and assured the customer that internal
   action would be taken against the concerned parties.
   -

   Offered a *replacement with Meller sunglass* within the eligible capped
   value.
   -

   The customer accepted the resolution and confirmed satisfaction.


*Gap Identified:*

*PRG Voice – Policy Knowledge & Call Handling Failure*

   1.

   *Advisor Shivaji Namdev (Case ID: 115140267):*
   -

      Provided *incorrect policy information* regarding brand exchange
      despite both frames falling under the ₹5,000 cap.
      -

      Failed to support the store while the customer was present and
*disconnected
      the call when handed to the customer*, with no callback or ownership.
      -

      This directly led to in-store escalation and customer distress.
      2.

   *Advisor Komal Gupta (Case ID: 115140653):*
   -

      Reiterated the *same incorrect policy interpretation* due to lack of
      awareness of the updated warranty policy.
      -

      Did not attempt de-escalation or escalation even after the customer
      threatened legal action.
      -

      Missed the opportunity to clarify policy correctly and resolve the
      issue at the first interaction.


*Regards,*
*Suraj Verma*

*Team - CEO Escalation *[image: 87Hq.gif]

On December 28, 2025 at 23:00 GMT, jaya pahwa <jayapahwa000@gmail.com>

Dear Sir/Madam,

This is in continuation of my repeated calls to your customer care,
interactions with your AI chatbot, conversations with your representive on
WhatsApp, and even a physical visit to your store at Sector 122, Noida,
all regarding the exchange request pertaining to John Jacobs sunglasses
bearing Product ID 134949.

The said sunglasses (without power) were purchased for Rs. 5000 under a
“Buy one get one free” offer along with another pair of specs of similar
price from your Select City Mall, Delhi Outlet on 25th December 2025 and
were delivered to me the very next day.

At the time of purchase, your store representative had categorically
expressly and assured that the company permits  a one time exchange of the
product if found unsatisfactory or for any reason, against any other
product available in the store. It was further clarified that only in case
the replacement product was of a higher value, I would be required to pay
the differential amount.

After receipt of the sunglasses, I found them unsuitable for my face
structure and accordingly initiated an exchange request through the
application. However, the exchange options displayed were limited to
significantly cheaper products, priced between ₹500-₹2000, and confined
only to Vincent and Lenskart brands. No options from Miller or Jacobs i.e.,
the premium category to which the purchased product belonged, were made
available. Further, the application did not even provide a search option to
explore other eligible products for exchange.

I therefore attempted to contact your customer care on multiple occasions;
however, I was only met with prolonged waiting tones and was repeatedly
kept on hold for 30-40 minutes at a time, without any meaningful assistance
or resultion. Similarly, AI chat bot offered only limited and generic
options and failed even to comprehend the issue, let alone provide any
resolution. Further, after multiple attempts, a representative who
initiated conversation on WhatsApp abruptly closed the chat stating
issue pertains
to another department, without transferring issue or offering any
assistance whatsoever.


Left with no alternative, I visited your Sector 122 Noida Store. The store
representative there accepted and examined the sunglasses and thereafter,
took an Ito for accepting exchange and  asked me to select an alternative
product from the Miller or John Jacobs range for exchange. Accordingly, I
selected a Miller product having Id 238521. However, at the time of
invoicing, representative himself was taken aback to find that the system
was demanding an additional payment of approximately Rs. 2600/-, despite the
selected product being of the same price range (Rs. 5000) and covered
under same
offer.

Thereafter, the store representative contacted the backend team, who stated
that an exchange for a Miller product was not possible, as it is
considered a separate brand. When I pointed out that exchanges with Vincent
products were allowed, the representative attempted to justify the
discrepancy by claiming that Vincent is an in-house brand, whereas Miller
is not. Upon questioning why such a restriction was not mentioned in the
exchange policy, the representative merely stated that my feedback for
policy had been noted, offering no resolution or explanation for omission
in policy.

Despite completing all requisite formalities and complying with the
exchange policy, the exchange of the product could not be effected. In view
of the foregoing, it is evident that there has been a clear deficiency in
service, caused by inconsistent application of your exchange policy, lack
of clarity in terms, false marketing as the advertisements also specify
free exchange for no reason, unresponsive customer care, and failure to
provide a timely resolution leading to further harassment which is
unacceptable for a brand of your standing. I therefore demand that my
exchange request be processed immediately in accordance with the assurances
given at the time of purchase, without any additional payment, and that a
written confirmation of the same be provided at the earliest.In the absence
of a prompt resolution, I shall be constrained to explore appropriate legal
remedies at your risk as to costs and consequences.

I expect a clear response within a reasonable time.

Yours faithfully,
Adv. Jaya Pahwa

Bonum Lex

C-12, Chirag Enclave,

G.K-1, New Delhi 110048
Mb.8178444588

emails.body:
Hi Team,

The RCA is already shared on the duplicate email thread.



*Observation:*Order ID 1316612980 was placed on 12th August 2025 for two
eyeglasses and one pair of sunglasses from Lenskart Jalahalli, Bengaluru
store.

On 15th December 2025, the customer reported a side hinge breakage in the
rimless frame (Product ID: 225542) and visited the Rajajinagar, Bengaluru
store (LKST1514) for repair.

The store team refused to repair the frame, resulting in a poor customer
experience. The customer reported unprofessional behavior, including
arrogance and lack of assistance from the store staff.

Additionally, the Store Manager issued a handwritten note on plain paper
stating “This frame can’t be repaired,” which was inappropriate and not
aligned with standard Lenskart processes.

On 16th December 2025, the customer visited Basaveshwaranagar Store
(LKST2328), where the store team raised an approval request.

Abhishek Kumar

the vendor, and their assessment is that only exposure to an acidic
material or certain adhesives coming into contact with the frame could

emails.snippet: Hi Maheswari, The team has not yet concluded the RCA for this case. They attempted to replicate the defect as described by the customer but were unable to remove the coating from the lens or frame
emails.body:
Hi Maheswari,

The team has not yet concluded the RCA for this case. They attempted to
replicate the defect as described by the customer but were unable to remove
the coating from the lens or frame using only the Lenskart lens cleaning
solution. This is why Kiran has requested the physical product for further
investigation.

The frame has an electroplated silver finish, and in this case, the entire
electroplating has peeled off along with the hard coating layer on the
lenses. Since the same cleaning solution is used across all fitting and
store QC processes for both frames and lenses, this issue is unusual.

We need to inspect the physical product to understand the defect better and
escalate it to the vendor with clear evidence.

@Karan Kumar <karan.kumar@lenskart.mobi> I discussed this yesterday with
you as well.

Regards,

Ruchi Nagpal

emails.body:
Hi Karan,

*Tomorrow we have a CEO escalation meeting, and we need some updates in the
sheet. Warehouse and local fitting should have separate tags, and under
product quality, dispatch delay and delivery delay should also be tagged
separately. This will help us in weekly reviews.  *

*Please find below summary of CEO Escalation data for the month of Nov'25:*
[image: image.png]

Note- For local fitting only count has been added, RCA status not added

Also please find the below short RCA Summary of these cases:

*Product Quality RCA:*
*Issue-1:*Recurring frame loose issues -1313526199 (Both PIDs) -Exceptional
case because low return % observed ( 5.95% & 5.38%)- inventory ok, hinge
cycle test passed
*Issue-2:* Alignment Issue -1323041202 - Fitter & QC operator Gap; Training
given
*Issue-3:*Product color coating issue-1322687085 -QC operator missed &
Manufacturing defect ;Inventory ok & Training given to QC operator
*Issue-4:*Scratches on the frame & Alignment Issue -1323130961 & 1322920025
(FR0 Product) ;Inventory ok & Training given to QC operator
*Issue-5: *Scratches on the Lens -1323434344 - QC operator Gap; Training
given
*Issue-6:* Product developed rust at temple tip- 1299667283 - It seems an
exceptional case of product quality because SST Passed and low return %
observed (2.2%)

*Usage/ Breakage/Handling:*
*Issue-1:*Scratches on the frame (1 M)- 1319934810 - It appears that the
frame and lenses have come in contact with a hard surface, causing the
marks observed
*Issue-2:*Temple broken from the hinge Junction (6.5 M) -1309302718 - This
might be broken due to mishandling
*Issue-3:*Coating issue on frame & Thickness issue (7 Days) - 1320785028 -
Coating issue is due to mishandling, and for the thickness, cx is comparing
it with a non-LK product after multiple exchanges
*Issue-4:*Left nose pad broken with arm from the nose bridge (9 M) -
1304396159 -  This might be broken due to mishandling
*Issue-5:* Scratches generated over the lenses (8 M)- 1307085247 - The
scratches generated over the lenses post usage
*Issue-6:* Frame Rim split (Frame screws damage and separated 3M) -
1318713339- Frame rim broken from the temporal down side. It looks like a
mishandling case

Perception:
*Issue-1:*Scratches on the hinge junction-1322601808 - The defect is
present on the frame temple near the hinge, which falls under the C zone
and is within SOP

Out of Warranty:
*Issue-1:*Pid colour turned yellow -1284620914 (1.8 Yrs) - Both lenses have
coating damage which is wear & tear case

Contact Lens Quality Issue:
*Issue-1:*CL damaged -1323574721 -In warehouse, QC operator checks the
quantity, expiry date, packet condition and the power mentioned on the
label. Open box QC is not allowed. Asked Suraj that after discussing with

This is an old complaint which my team received on 23rd Nov'25 from
Maheswari. While it has already been solved for the customer - this has
also been cross checked from Plant's side as well and they have shared a
stringent feedback with the QC operators.

   QC failure. However, the team failed to correctly mark the item as QC
   failed - within 72 hrs, instead initiating the standard exchange process.
   While the exchange was completed timely, this procedural error compromises
   the accurate systematic record of whether the product passed the QC or
   failed.

> On Fri, Nov 21, 2025 at 12:48 PM Manoj Lonar <manoj.lonar@lenskart.in>
> wrote:
>
>> Hi,
>>
>> Please find the RCA details below;
>>
>> Root Cause:
>> During the creation of an exchange order, the system fetches the shipping
>> address and exchange cart via separate APIs. In rare cases, the
>> Shipping/Exchange API calls may time out, which leads to the issue
>> encountered.
>> We have a fallback mechanism in place that redirects the user to the
>> Homepage when such failures occur, to prevent a broken experience.
>>
>> Fix / Improvements:
>> Since then, we have implemented several optimizations in the Exchange
>> flow, which should significantly reduce the chances of this scenario
>> happening again.
>>
>> Reproduction Status:
>> We were not able to reproduce the issue on our side, but we will continue
>> to monitor the flow closely.
>>
>> Thank you!
>>

emails.body:
Hi,

Please find the RCA details below;

Root Cause:
During the creation of an exchange order, the system fetches the shipping
address and exchange cart via separate APIs. In rare cases, the
Shipping/Exchange API calls may time out, which leads to the issue
encountered.
We have a fallback mechanism in place that redirects the user to the
Homepage when such failures occur, to prevent a broken experience.

Fix / Improvements:
Since then, we have implemented several optimizations in the Exchange flow,
which should significantly reduce the chances of this scenario happening
again.

Reproduction Status:
We were not able to reproduce the issue on our side, but we will continue
to monitor the flow closely.

Thank you!

>

emails.snippet: Hey Maheswari, While this does make sense...
emails.body:
Hey Maheswari,

While this does make sense, I'd like to add on -

For pointer 1) As far as I am aware, the package's weight is indeed tracked
upon dispatch & delivery. For better insights, we can consult +Rachit Jain
<rachit.jain@lenskart.in>  for guidance on leveraging this data point as a
tracking and verification tool for handling cases of such nature.

For pointer 2) We did request this customer provide an unboxing video, but
he was unable to, stating they had not recorded one. He was also fumed by
hearing this request, pointing out that our website/application does not
require or mention the need for an unboxing video.

On Mon, Nov 17, 2025 at 2:37 PM Maheswari M <maheswari.m@lenskart.com>
wrote:

> Hi Karan,
>
> Thanks for the detailed RCA, here are my observations.
>
> 1. Can we also please include weight as one parameter while we pack and
> ship the order and cross check it on the delivery side and when the
> customer raises an issue.  We need to discuss the scale of the weighing
> machine, but I think this kind of issue will keep popping up in the future
> also where customers complain about empty parcels.
> 2. For all the COD and home-delivery orders, can we please request the
> customer to share opening box video ( This needs to have a lot of
> discussions, but an option to try out)
>
>
>
>
>

>> Hi Rachit,
>>
>> This is the same customer who came in reporting Empty Parcel in Oct'25.
>> Here's the RCA for his case.
>>
>> Customer Name: Alok Shrivastava
>>
>> Order ID: 1322118332
>>
>> Sale Source: Online (COD)
>>
>> Order Date: 25th October 2025
>>
>>
>> MVC Score:
>>
>> [image: image.png]
>>
>>
>>
>> Concern: Received empty parcel delivery
>>
>> Observation (At CS Level):
>>
>>
>>    - The order 1322118332 was placed online under Cash on Delivery (COD)
>>    mode on 25th October 2025 and delivered within the timeline on 29th October
>>    2025.
>>    - On 29th October, the customer reached out via chatbot and raised a
>>    refund request for an empty parcel under case ID 112376059.
>>    - The customer later connected with Advisor Rashmi Sinha, who
>>    informed that COD orders are not eligible for direct refunds. The customer
>>    requested a callback, which was arranged immediately, and ticket ID
>>    112378572 was raised for the empty parcel/delivery dispute.
>>    - The customer again requested a callback, which was provided. The
>>    advisor extended an apology and shared a TAT of 31st October; however, the
>>    customer refused to wait.
>>    - The chat was then escalated to L2 Advisor Divanshi Ratra, as the
>>    customer insisted on an instant resolution. Divanshi apologized,
>>    explained the process, and requested 24 hours, but the customer continued
>>    to deny waiting or allowing investigation.
>>    - Later the same day, the customer initiated another chat which again
>>    got assigned to Rashmi Sinha, who reiterated the 31st October TAT, raised a
>>    ticket, and closed the chat.
>>    - The customer then escalated the issue to the CEO Desk on 29th
>>    October under case ID 112381223, reporting the same concern.
>>
>> Action Taken (Post CEO Escalation):
>>
>>
>> We got this crosschecked from both the warehouse & Logistics team. Here’s
>> their observations -
>>
>> Warehouse team’s RCA:
>>
>>
>>    - The team shared the QC & Dispatch CCTV footage which clearly showed
>>    that the product was correctly packed and shipped from our end.
>>
>> Logistica team’s RCA:
>>
>>
>>    - The aligned courier FE from Bluedart confirmed that this customer
>>    had booked 3 different orders from Lenskart and all of them were on COD.
>>    - Initially he was prolonging the delivery, but on 29th Oct, he
>>    agreed to take one product out of 3.
>>    - During the time of collection, the packaging was intact and the
>>    customer didn’t report any issues with it.
>>
>> - The customer was informed about the findings we had from our
>> investigation - which claims that the product was correctly dispatched &
>> delivered from our end.
>>
>> - However, since the order value was quite low (Rs. 600) we made an
>> exception for this customer and offered the same product as a replacement
>> under new order ID: 1322485578.
>>
>> - To our surprise, the customer again reported Empty Parcel against the
>> compensatory order we placed for him.
>>
>> - At the time of delivery, he was abusing the courier FE which led to a
>> heated argument between the customer and the courier FE (which the customer
>> has highlighted in his email).
>>
>> - Despite knowing we delivered the product correctly twice, just to close
>> it for the customer as he was spamming us on Email & Social Channels, we
>> offered a refund of Rs. 600 as the final resolution from our end.
>>
>> Final stance from our end:
>>
>>
>>    - The customer seeks compensation for the time he invested in all the
>>    follow ups he has been taking and the inconveniences he faced.
>>    - We informed the customer that despite delivering the order
>>    correctly from our end - not once but twice, we offered a refund to him to
>>    ensure his satisfaction. However, since Lenskart has no compensatory
>>    policies, we won’t be able to cater this request.
>>    - This resolution has already been conveyed from our end and the case
>>    stands closed. However, this customer spam us every now and then to seek
>>    compensation.
>>
>>

>>
>>    - *Escalated Interaction Style: *Customer exhibits a pattern of

ship the order and cross check it on the delivery side and when the
customer raises an issue.  We need to discuss the scale of the weighing
machine, but I think this kind of issue will keep popping up in the future
also where customers complain about empty parcels.
2. For all the COD and home-delivery orders, can we please request the
customer to share opening box video ( This needs to have a lot of
discussions, but an option to try out)

emails.body:
Hi Rachit,

This is the same customer who came in reporting Empty Parcel in Oct'25.
Here's the RCA for his case.

Customer Name: Alok Shrivastava

Order ID: 1322118332

Sale Source: Online (COD)

Order Date: 25th October 2025


MVC Score:

[image: image.png]



Concern: Received empty parcel delivery

Observation (At CS Level):


   - The order 1322118332 was placed online under Cash on Delivery (COD)
   mode on 25th October 2025 and delivered within the timeline on 29th October
   2025.
   - On 29th October, the customer reached out via chatbot and raised a
   refund request for an empty parcel under case ID 112376059.
   - The customer later connected with Advisor Rashmi Sinha, who informed
   that COD orders are not eligible for direct refunds. The customer requested
   a callback, which was arranged immediately, and ticket ID 112378572 was
   raised for the empty parcel/delivery dispute.
   - The customer again requested a callback, which was provided. The
   advisor extended an apology and shared a TAT of 31st October; however, the
   customer refused to wait.
   - The chat was then escalated to L2 Advisor Divanshi Ratra, as the
   customer insisted on an instant resolution. Divanshi apologized,
   explained the process, and requested 24 hours, but the customer continued
   to deny waiting or allowing investigation.
   - Later the same day, the customer initiated another chat which again
   got assigned to Rashmi Sinha, who reiterated the 31st October TAT, raised a
   ticket, and closed the chat.
   - The customer then escalated the issue to the CEO Desk on 29th October
   under case ID 112381223, reporting the same concern.

Action Taken (Post CEO Escalation):


We got this crosschecked from both the warehouse & Logistics team. Here’s
their observations -

Warehouse team’s RCA:


   - The team shared the QC & Dispatch CCTV footage which clearly showed
   that the product was correctly packed and shipped from our end.

Logistica team’s RCA:


   - The aligned courier FE from Bluedart confirmed that this customer had
   booked 3 different orders from Lenskart and all of them were on COD.
   - Initially he was prolonging the delivery, but on 29th Oct, he agreed
   to take one product out of 3.
   - During the time of collection, the packaging was intact and the
   customer didn’t report any issues with it.

- The customer was informed about the findings we had from our
investigation - which claims that the product was correctly dispatched &
delivered from our end.

- However, since the order value was quite low (Rs. 600) we made an
exception for this customer and offered the same product as a replacement
under new order ID: 1322485578.

- To our surprise, the customer again reported Empty Parcel against the
compensatory order we placed for him.

- At the time of delivery, he was abusing the courier FE which led to a
heated argument between the customer and the courier FE (which the customer
has highlighted in his email).

- Despite knowing we delivered the product correctly twice, just to close
it for the customer as he was spamming us on Email & Social Channels, we
offered a refund of Rs. 600 as the final resolution from our end.

Final stance from our end:


   - The customer seeks compensation for the time he invested in all the
   follow ups he has been taking and the inconveniences he faced.
   - We informed the customer that despite delivering the order correctly
   from our end - not once but twice, we offered a refund to him to ensure his
   satisfaction. However, since Lenskart has no compensatory policies, we
   won’t be able to cater this request.
   - This resolution has already been conveyed from our end and the case
   stands closed. However, this customer spam us every now and then to seek
   compensation.


*Customer Tendency & Escalation Patterns:*

   - *Escalated Interaction Style: *Customer exhibits a pattern of verbal
   abuse toward L1 support agents, frequently necessitating supervisor
   intervention to de-escalate the interaction.
   - *Non-Adherence to Standard Process:* Consistently attempts to bypass
   standard operational procedures and service level agreements (SLAs),
   prolonging interactions across all channels (Chat/Calls).
   - *Coercive Escalation Threat:* When standard requests are denied, the
   customer leverages threats of external exposure (e.g., contacting executive
   leadership or public social media complaints) to attempt to force
   concessions for non-standard demands.
